measures.definition: Σ Quantity × (UnitPrice − NetPrice). The account is knowledge/discount.md.
What one currency was worth in another on one day: 100,450 quoted rates over a date and an ordered pair of currencies. The account is knowledge/exchange_rate.md.
What Contoso would have charged at list: quantity times the undiscounted price, per sale, summed. The account is knowledge/gross_revenue.md.
Σ Quantity × (NetPrice − UnitCost), identical to Revenue − COGS. The account is knowledge/margin.md.
What Contoso actually charged: quantity times the discounted price, per sale, summed. The account is knowledge/net_revenue.md.
What the goods on a sale cost Contoso: quantity times unit cost, per sale, summed. The account is knowledge/sales_cost.md.
How many items went out: the quantity on a sale, summed. The account is knowledge/units_sold.md.

kinds.governs: Identity / matching / scoping of an entity from the question (name, code, key, definition).
Measure math — additivity, period bounds, grain (how a measure may be summed/read).
What to assume when an axis is unspecified but a safe default exists.
An underspecified REQUIRED dimension — ASK, never guess.
What to filter out / never include (pseudo-entries, unmapped rows, stale vintages).
A fact the consumer INHERITS from the serving view (relied on, not re-derived).

catalog.when: a question counts, lists or filters this concept's rows
catalog.then: 2 named population(s) of one axis: `real`; `sentinel`. a question naming none of them takes `real`, and the answer DISCLOSES that it did. this default holds only when the question is ABOUT this concept — a concept merely on the join path keeps none of it
catalog.never: mixing two readings of one axis in a single figure; reporting a count over all rows as a count of the default reading

catalog.when: a measure is grouped by or filtered on this concept and the question does not say through what
catalog.then: 4 named reading(s): `customer` (also called customer country; where our customers are; customer countries; where the buyer is); `location` (also called site country; location country); `store` (also called store country; where we trade; trading country); `territory` (also called country of the sale; where the sale was made; trade in; business in; market). `customer` arrives by `customer__based_in__country`; `location` arrives by `location__in__country`; `store` arrives by `store__trades_in__country`; `territory` arrives by `net_revenue__attributed_to__country`. a question naming none of them takes `territory`, and the answer DISCLOSES that it did
catalog.never: averaging two readings, which are answers to different questions; picking between them silently

catalog.when: a rate, share or percentage over this measure is asked for
catalog.then: 1 named ratio(s): `percent` (also called discount percentage; discount rate; discount %; discount as a percentage). `percent` divides by GrossRevenue. a question naming none of them takes `percent`, and the answer DISCLOSES that it did
catalog.never: dividing by a figure this bundle has not declared

catalog.then: across a categorical axis it is none; across a time axis it is average. It may not be summed across ANY declared axis. Apply the declared effect and say which was applied
catalog.never: summing `rate` across a categorical or time axis; weighting every member of an axis equally when the declaration says otherwise

catalog.never: constraining or grouping on `to_currency` without `from_currency`; treating two rows with the same code and different scope as one thing

catalog.when: a question names this concept and does not say which reading it means

catalog.when: a question neither names a window nor constrains this axis's own period column(s)
catalog.then: 1 named window(s): `all_time`. `all_time` is unbounded — no period predicate at all. a question naming none of them takes `all_time`, and the answer DISCLOSES that it did
catalog.never: reporting a defaulted answer without disclosing the extent it covered, which is indistinguishable from a guess; applying a default to a question that has already constrained this axis's own period column — its statement governs, and nothing is disclosed about it

catalog.when: an anchor for "now" is needed over this relation — a declared window pins its period to one, or the bundle's vintage is recorded from one
catalog.then: resolve it to `MAX(order_date)` over the whole of `contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line`, this relation declaring no axis to pin — which the canon permits only where there is none, and DISCLOSE the date the answer anchored to
catalog.never: anchoring on the clock date instead of the latest date the data carries; leaving the anchor unscoped on a relation that does carry a plan, budget or scenario axis: an unscoped MAX returns the planning horizon, not the latest actual; lowering this anchor into a relative window on its own: the anchor is a DATE, the window it stands for needs a grain, and inventing one answers about a different span than the question asked

edges.join_rule: v_contoso5_sales_line.order_date = v_contoso5_fx_rate.date_day AND v_contoso5_sales_line.currency_code = v_contoso5_fx_rate.to_currency AND v_contoso5_fx_rate.from_currency = 'USD'
edges.notes:
THE PREDICATE IS DECLARED, AND THE `1` IS MEASURED — operator-approved 2026-10-08. It was prose until today, held out of `join_rule` so it would not "stand as an unmeasured claim"; the cost of that was larger than the claim. `planner/sql.py` reads an edge with no `join_rule` as a SAME-TABLE edge ("no physical JOIN needed"), marks both relations joined and emits NO ON clause — so the predicate was not merely unverified, it was unreachable, and the `composite_key_guard` bound on the rule can only fire on SQL that mentions `to_currency`, which such a plan never does. An enforcement half with no realization half.
MEASURED 2026-10-08 against contoso5.duckdb, all 223 974 served lines: the triple returns EXACTLY ONE rate per line — rows_out 223 974, min 1, max 1, 0 violations, 0 unmatched on every one of the five currencies (USD 113 614, EUR 49 203, CAD 24 250, GBP 22 829, AUD 14 078). That 1:1 is what `cardinality: '1'` now asserts, and it replaces the rule's former `never: join on currency alone` with a number: on currency alone the join returns up to 20 090 rates per line (every day that currency was quoted), on date alone 25 (the 25 ordered pairs quoted that day). The rule's old prose cited "100 450 rows of it", which is the relation's SIZE and not any fan-out.
`from_currency = 'USD'` IS NOT A CHOSEN LITERAL. It is the amounts' declared unit — net_revenue.yaml#grounding.source.columns.net_amount.offers.aggregate.unit — so the pin is checkable against a declaration rather than being magic. Confirmed independently 2026-10-08 (acceptance/verification/manual_value_check_2026-10-08.md): net_amount is USD on every line regardless of `currency_code`, which is the currency TRANSACTED IN and not the unit of the figure. This edge therefore converts USD amounts OUT to a local currency on request; it is never the way to "get USD", and nothing should multiply net_amount by this rate to obtain one.
STILL OWED: `tools/mac_measure_edges.py` matches `a.x = b.y` only (its own refusal text), so this edge stays in the generator's `unmeasurable` list with a new reason and carries no `verified_by` yet — a ref to a record that does not exist would be the dangling-reference defect. The measurement above is reproducible from the SQL in the commit message.

104,990 customers over 8 of the 9 codes, no nulls; the ninth is `--`, the online sentinel, which no customer carries. PARENT OPTIONAL, hence `0..N` and not `1..N`: a country with no customer exists, and check_edge_claims_proved refused the stronger claim (2026-09-30).
74 store rows over all 9 codes, no nulls, mandatory both ways — the store table is where the country set comes from, the online row's `--` included.
67 locations over all 9 codes, mandatory both ways. Location keeps its own `country_name` column, which is the SAME fact one hop closer; the name's home is Country.
67 locations behind 74 store rows, mandatory both ways.
Two edges to Currency because the pair is ORDERED and inverting it is wrong by the rate squared.
